newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania resumes ferry services to eastern Congo. [CORRECTED 11:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Tanzania resumes ferry services to eastern Congo. [CORRECTED 11:00 GMT]

text.p: State-run Tanzania Railways Corporation (TRC) said on Friday it had resumed ferry services to the eastern region of the Democratic Republic of the Congo interrupted last year by the civil war.
"Sailing was stopped as soon as political instability started in eastern (Zaire) Congo," said Livingstone Chipindula, assistant chief commercial manager of the TRC.
"It's now resumed. It's an extremely popular and viable service -- a lot of demand for transport both cargo and passengers," he added.
Chipindula told Reuters that a once weekly service had now commenced from Kigoma port on Lake Tanganyika to Uvira and Kalemie in the Congo.

The TRC's workhorse on the lake service is the venerable MV Liemba, now in its 81st year of operation. A familiar sight on Lake Tanganyika, the historic Liemba is licensed to carry 600 passengers and 250 tonnes (corrects from 250 kgs) of deck cargo, Chipindula said.

"Passengers and shippers are urged to utilise the TRC marine services plying the waters of Lake Tanganyika both for adventure and business missions to the neighbouring state," said a TRC news release marking the resumption of services.
